findings.issue_text: [BUG] The per-iteration cleanup registers removal of an IDP with alias "alias" instead of the actual created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so the cleanup removes nothing. All 20 created IDPs leak into the shared test realm across the test run; the admin-client proxy resource for non-existent alias "alias" makes remove() a silent no-op, polluting subsequent organization/IDP tests and intermittently breaking unrelated test ordering.

[BUG] The cleanup for the newly created "idp-alias-20" likewise calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, referencing a non-existent alias. idp-alias-20 (later made login-available and org-linked by the test itself) is never cleaned up, leaking a broker with BROKER_PUBLIC=true into the realm for subsequent tests in the same suite.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate stage dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard, and the predicate is invoked by registerIDPLoginInvalidation on models obtained from idpDelegate (create/remove/update paths) rather than only from the login query path it was written for. Any IdentityProviderModel returned by the delegate with a non-null organizationId but a null config map (representations built via setters without config) throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate during create/update/remove, turning IDP admin operations into 500s.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the cleanup resource lookup returns null and the method reference `null::remove` throws a NullPointerException during test cleanup. Test teardown fails after the assertions pass, breaking the test run and leaving 20 identity providers and the organization links un-cleaned, poisoning subsequent tests in the same realm.

[BUG] The second cleanup registration for the newly created idp-alias-20 repeats the literal-alias copy-paste, registering `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` instead of "idp-alias-20". The NPE-during-cleanup described above fires here too, and even if it survived, idp-alias-20 (which the test later mutates across all invalidation scenarios) is never removed from the realm.

[ADVISORY] The new cache-extension branch in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin (existing IdentityProviderListQuery whose getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, triggering invalidateObject + query-with-previous merge) has no test coverage: the test queries each FetchMode with exactly one organizationId value, so the multi-searchKey path (e.g. ORG_ONLY for org A then ORG_ONLY for org B under the same cacheKey) is never exercised. A regression in the query-merge/`cache.getCurrentCounter()` revision logic (which differs from the first-branch `startupRevision`) ships undetected; clusters with multiple organizations will serve a wrong or stale IDP list on the second organization's login page.

[ADVISORY] The self-healing fallback branch in getForLogin — a cached internalId that resolves to null via getById, causing registerInvalidation(cacheKey) and a delegate reload — is never triggered or verified by any test in the diff. If this recovery path misbehaves (e.g. invalidates only the local node's cache key without cluster-wide propagation), a cache poisoned by a deleted IDP's id would serve a permanently broken login page on that node with no test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The newly added `idp.isEnabled()` re-filter in both branches of searchForIdentityProviders — added because a wrapped/cached IDP can appear in getForLogin results while disabled — has no test in the diff verifying that a disabled-then-cached IDP no longer renders on the organization login page. Other callers of getForLogin that don't re-check isEnabled (any broker-selection path outside this bean) still receive the disabled IDP from the cached stream; nothing in this diff pins the contract of which layer is responsible for the enablement check.

[BUG] The getLoginPredicate change (requiring orgId==null or BROKER_PUBLIC config) silently alters the semantics of getForLogin for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation and every caller of the predicate, not just the caching layer this PR claims to add. Storage providers with no cache (e.g. map/JPA in non-cached setups) and any other consumer of getLoginPredicate (admin/console listing, other SPI callers) now exclude organization-linked non-public IDPs that were previously returned; this is a cross-cutting behavior change not traceable to the 'add caching support' requirement, and it is hidden inside what looks like a cache-only diff — additionally, idp.getConfig() returning null for a model with an organizationId throws NPE inside the predicate.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) while the cache-miss path maps results through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the returned stream has different semantics depending on cache state. The first uncached call after invalidation returns organization-wrapped IDP models (which can override enabled/visibility per organization context), while all subsequent cached calls return unwrapped raw models — callers like OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean get different data for the identical request depending on whether the cache was warm; the method does not enforce the invariant that its result shape is independent of cache state.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual generated alias "idp-alias-" + i, and duplicates it for every loop iteration. getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) either throws EntityNotFoundException during cleanup or is a silent no-op for all 21 created IDPs, leaving test data in the shared test realm and polluting subsequent tests that read realm IDPs via the new login caches.

[ADVISORY] The update-path invalidation optimization (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) relies on the assumption that the organizationId field and BROKER_PUBLIC config on the passed models capture every way an IDP's login eligibility can change, which the diff does not establish. Any write path that mutates login-relevant state without passing through this provider's update() (e.g. organization link changes driven through OrganizationProvider's own broker update, or direct config changes by other SPIs) leaves the .idp.login caches serving stale IDP lists until an unrelated invalidation; the skip-fast branch converts a previously-always-fresh lookup into a staleness window that the new test only exercises through the admin API.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw (unwrapped) IdentityProviderModel objects while the delegate path wraps each result with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the same call returns differently-behaving models depending on whether the entry was already cached. The login page's IDP list changes behavior between the first (uncached) request and every subsequent (cached) request after the cache warms: organization-aware wrapping (which the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean diff explicitly acknowledges alters visibility/enabled semantics — 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped') is missing on the cached path, producing different IDP lists and enabled flags for the same realm/org depending on cache state.

[BUG] The new predicate arm `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, and getConfig() can be null for programmatically created IdentityProviderModel instances. Any IDP with an organizationId set but a null config map makes getLoginPredicate().test(idp) throw NullPointerException, breaking every caller of getForLogin/getLoginSearchOptions for that realm, including non-cached storage providers that now inherit the new predicate arm.

[ADVISORY] The change to getLoginPredicate silently alters the results of getForLogin for ALL IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations (including JPA/Map with no cache), not just the new caching path — org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC=true are now excluded by a shared SPI predicate where the filtering was previously the caller's concern. Existing deployments and any in-tree or out-of-tree caller that relied on getForLogin returning org-linked non-public brokers (e.g. custom login UIs, OIDC well-known endpoints) see their IDP lists shrink with no version bump or migration note; behavior is baked into the SPI rather than the FetchMode/caller layer where ORG_ONLY vs ALL semantics live.

[ADVISORY] remove(alias) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a delegate/DB query) before the cache-validity check, even in the branch where the cached entry was previously sufficient for the internalId invalidation. Every alias removal pays an uncached delegate lookup it did not pay before, solely to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation; in a single-node Map storage setup this converts a cache-served admin operation into a hot DB hit, and when the IDP is not found the storedIdp passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidation is null (handled, but the wasted query remains).

[ADVISORY] A single cache entry keyed by (realm, FetchMode) accumulates a searchKey->IDP-set map for every organizationId ever queried, with whole-entry rebuild (invalidateObject + full delegate reload + addRevisioned) on each first query for a new org and whole-entry invalidation on any IDP change, so entry size and rebuild cost grow linearly with the number of organizations. A realm with many organizations (Keycloak targets org-heavy tenants) gets one ever-growing cache object that is fully reloaded from the delegate each time a new org's login page is first hit, and fully invalidated (cold reload for all orgs) on any single IDP create/update/remove of a login IDP — a thundering-herd style scalability cliff on the login path the cache was meant to accelerate.

[ADVISORY] The two cache-population branches are asymmetric: the first uses addRevisioned(query, startupRevision) while the second (searchKey miss on an existing entry) uses cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) after having captured loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey) in between an invalidateObject and the re-add, so the revision embedded in the query and the version used for the re-add can disagree. If the counter raced with a concurrent cluster invalidation between getCurrentRevision and getCurrentCounter, the entry is installed with a version that makes subsequent invalidation checks (isInvalid comparisons against the embedded revision) pass for stale data, leaving a login page serving pre-invalidations IDP lists; the inconsistency between the two branches also invites drift on the next copy of this pattern.

[ADVISORY] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" (get("alias")::remove) instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so it targets a nonexistent identity provider. The 20 created IDPs (and later idp-alias-20) are never removed by cleanup, polluting the test realm for subsequent tests and, depending on the admin client, causing the cleanup itself to throw a 404/NullPointerException during test teardown.

[BUG] The shared SPI's getLoginPredicate() was silently redefined to exclude organization-linked identity providers lacking BROKER_PUBLIC, changing the semantics of getForLogin for every storage provider and caller, not just the caching layer. This PR's stated intent is adding caching; instead it alters core login-visibility semantics for all implementations (JPA/map/legacy) and any other caller of getLoginPredicate() — org-linked private IDPs that previously appeared in getForLogin results for their own organization members disappear, with no human sign-off that the objective expanded from caching to a behavior change.

[BUG] The login page bean now filters out IDPs whose wrapped model reports isEnabled()==false, changing which identity providers render on the organization login page. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel instances that are disabled (e.g. private org brokers) were previously passed to createIdentityProvider and now vanish from the login page for all users; this is a user-visible login-page behavior change bundled into a caching PR without explicit acceptance of the changed objective.

[BUG] The cached-hit path of getForLogin returns IDPs fetched via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the cache-miss and invalidation fallback paths do wrap, so the same request returns differently-shaped (non-organization-aware) models depending on cache state. The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean already had to re-check isEnabled() 'as idp might have been wrapped' (companion hunk in this diff); on cache hits the login page instead receives unwrapped models whose organization-linked behavior (e.g. redirect/alias handling for org members vs. the public broker config gated by BROKER_PUBLIC) is lost, so an end user hitting the login page after a cache populate gets different/broken broker options than a user on the cold path.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate arm 'idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))' dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check and without consulting the organization provider's isBrokerPublic() logic, hard-coding the visibility rule into the storage SPI. Any IdentityProviderModel implementation (custom storage/legacy import) whose getConfig() returns null throws NullPointerException from getLoginPredicate, breaking every getForLogin call including the login page; and future changes to org-broker visibility semantics must now be replicated in two places (OrganizationProvider and this SPI predicate), risking a normalization-mismatch where the org provider treats an IDP as public while the login predicate does not, silently hiding it from the login page.

[ADVISORY] When an existing IdentityProviderListQuery lacks the requested organizationId searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then re-adds a merged query using cache.getCurrentCounter() as the revision rather than the startupRevision used on first population, so concurrent readers on other cluster nodes can observe a revision/counter pairing the invalidation protocol does not expect. Under concurrent logins against different organizations in a clustered deployment, a stale query object resurrected from the local Infinispan cache can be re-added with a revision that is not the session's startup revision, allowing the merge path to re-insert entries containing IDP ids invalidated earlier in the same transaction; users then see removed or disabled identity providers on the login page until the next full invalidation.

[BUG] The test registers cleanup against the wrong alias literal "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) dereferences a non-existent IdentityProviderResource. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns a resource for a nonexistent IDP; the cleanup remove() throws a 404 (or the resource is null causing an NPE), failing the test during cleanup and leaving the 20 created IDPs behind to pollute subsequent tests in the realm.

[ADVISORY] The new test never exercises the 'query exists but searchKey not cached' branch of getForLogin (the cached == null path that calls cache.invalidateObject, getCurrentRevision, and addRevisioned with cache.getCurrentCounter()). Every getForLogin call in the test uses the same organizationId per FetchMode, so the multi-organization sub-map merge path — which also uses getCurrentCounter instead of the startupRevision used by the first branch — is completely unverified; a regression there (stale or dropped IDP lists for a second organization hitting a warm cache) would ship unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] The test discards the return value of every session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) call and only asserts internal cache-query sizes, never the stream contents or their organization-aware wrapping. The caching layer could return wrong IdentityProviderModel instances (wrong models resolved by internal ID, missing createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping) or take the cache-miss fallback path (idp == null) and the test would still pass, since only the cache object's set sizes are checked — the actual user-visible behavior is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The isEnabled() re-check added to both filter chains in searchForIdentityProviders has no test in this diff that asserts a disabled-but-wrapped IDP is excluded from the login page. The stated reason for the change ('idp might have been wrapped' by the caching layer returning a model that bypasses the delegate's enabled filtering) is exactly the scenario the new test should cover but doesn't — OrganizationCacheTest never renders the login page nor asserts enabled/disabled filtering through the bean, so a regression reintroducing disabled IDPs on the org login page would pass the suite.

[ADVISORY] The change to getLoginPredicate silently reclassifies every existing org-linked identity provider without a BROKER_PUBLIC config entry as unavailable for login, with no backfill or migration step for stored IDP configs. Deploying this against existing realms drops all org-linked brokers that never had BROKER_PUBLIC explicitly set from every login page and every consumer of getLoginPredicate at once; operators see brokers disappear from the login screen with no data change, no migration, and no way to tell from the diff which existing rows are affected.

[BUG] The cleanup registration in testCacheIDPForLogin fetches the nonexistent alias "alias" (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so get("alias") returns null and the cleanup method reference throws NullPointerException during teardown. Both IDP-creation loops (lines ~390 and ~432) register a cleanup against a provider that does not exist, so test teardown throws an NPE and the 20+ created identity providers are never removed, leaking state into subsequent tests in the same realm.

[ADVISORY] In getForLogin's not-yet-cached-searchKey branch, the new IdentityProviderListQuery is added with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the initial-population branch uses the session's startupRevision, so the incrementally-added search entries are revisioned differently from the initial entry for the same cache key. A reader that populated a different searchKey for the same realm+fetchMode key gets a differently-revisioned query entry; if the revisioned-add semantics of getCurrentCounter do not match startupRevision-guarded invalidation, subsequent invalidations from registerIDPLoginInvalidation can leave a stale searchKey's IDP set live after an IDP is removed, serving a removed broker on the organization login page until the whole entry is evicted.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidation dereferences the passed IdentityProviderModel through getLoginPredicate (idp.getOrganizationId(), idp.getConfig()) without a null check, and in update() the idpById lookup result can be null when the internalId does not resolve. An update() call whose getById(internalId) returns null (e.g. alias was already removed, or an ID with no backing row) throws NullPointerException from the added predicate chain instead of the no-op that the pre-existing registerIDPInvalidation(null) path tolerated, turning a previously-benign update into a 500 for admins.

[BUG] The new predicate stage `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` throws NullPointerException whenever an IDP has a non-null organizationId and a null config map (IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns null when no config was ever set). Any call path that evaluates getLoginPredicate() — including the cache provider's create()/update()/remove() invalidation logic — crashes with NPE instead of completing; an admin creating/updating or a login flow listing IDPs for a realm where an org-linked IDP was imported without a config map gets a 500.

[ADVISORY] The cached hit path resolves IDs via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while the two delegate paths in the same method do apply it, so the returned model shape depends on whether the list query was already cached. Users hitting the warm cache get plain IdentityProviderModel instances while cold-cache users get organization-aware wrapped instances; any consumer relying on the wrapper's overridden behavior (e.g. the enabled flag re-check added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) sees different results for the same request depending on cache state.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares the updated model against `original` obtained from getById() which is served from the IDP-level Infinispan cache, so the skip decision is made on a possibly stale snapshot of the stored IDP. If the cached original is stale (e.g. a recent change from another node has not yet been reflected), the predicate comparison can wrongly conclude login-availability is unchanged and skip invalidating the login caches, leaving the login IDP list stale across cluster nodes until an unrelated invalidation fires.

[ADVISORY] Each distinct organizationId encountered for a given FetchMode causes the entire cached IdentityProviderListQuery to be invalidated (cache.invalidateObject) and rebuilt with the previous entries merged, so the single cache entry accumulates an unbounded per-org map and every new org's first login request evicts-and-rebuilds the entry for all orgs. In realms with many organizations, the first login per org pays a full delegate query plus a cluster-wide invalidation of the shared key, and the query object's internal map grows linearly with org count — cache churn and memory growth that degrade exactly the hot login path this diff intends to speed up.

[ADVISORY] The defensive re-check added to both branches only re-checks idp.isEnabled(), not the other criteria of the login predicate (hideOnLogin, org BROKER_PUBLIC), so a wrapped model that was made login-ineligible by any non-enabled criterion still passes the filter. A login page served from the cached getForLogin path can render an IDP that hideOnLogin or org-visibility rules exclude, and clicking it proceeds into a broker flow the admin explicitly hid — inconsistent with the predicate the cache is supposed to honor.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, after creating each IDP (including `idp-alias-20`), the test registers cleanup with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`. The string literal `"alias"` does not match the created aliases like `"idp-alias-20"`, so this cleanup will not remove the created broker(s). Since the test later updates `idp-alias-20` (including setting `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` and linking it to an org), failing to clean it up can leak state into subsequent tests in the same realm/suite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new stage to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that dereferences `idp.getConfig().get(...)` with no null guard: `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. The diff also expands usage of this predicate beyond the login query path by invoking it from `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` during `create/update/remove` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`. However, the claim that `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can be null (and thus will definitely cause NPEs/500s) is not verifiable from this diff alone; it depends on the contract/implementations of `IdentityProviderModel` not shown here. Still, the lack of a null-guard is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern given the broadened call sites.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, inside the loop creating `idp-alias-0` .. `idp-alias-19`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal "alias") instead of using the actual created alias (e.g., `"idp-alias-" + i`). This means the test teardown will not remove the created identity providers (and may repeatedly attempt to remove a non-existent/incorrect alias), leaving test data behind and potentially contaminating subsequent tests. The specific claim that `get(... )` returns null and causes `null::remove` NPE is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the incorrect cleanup target is clearly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second cleanup registration for the newly created idp-alias-20 repeats the literal-alias copy-paste, registering `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` instead of "idp-alias-20". The NPE-during-cleanup described above fires here too, and even if it survived, idp-alias-20 (which the test later mutates across all invalidation scenarios) is never removed from the realm.

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, both cleanup registrations use the hardcoded string `"alias"` instead of the actual created aliases. In the initial loop creating `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19`, it does `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, and later when creating `idp-alias-20` it repeats the same `get("alias")` cleanup. As a result, the test never registers cleanup for `idp-alias-20` (or any of the created IDPs), so they won't be removed after the test and cleanup may attempt to remove a non-existent/incorrect alias.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a non-trivial caching branch in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`: when a cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns `null`, it runs `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and stores a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)` using `cache.getCurrentCounter()` (different from the initial caching path using `startupRevision`). The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only ever calls `getForLogin` with `organizationId == null` and a single `orgaId`, so it never exercises the multi-`searchKey` path under the same `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` (e.g., ORG_ONLY for org A then ORG_ONLY for org B). Thus this new merge/revision branch has no direct test coverage, which is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a proven runtime bug.

If this recovery path misbehaves (e.g. invalidates only the local node's cache key without cluster-wide propagation), a cache poisoned by a deleted IDP's id would serve a permanently broken login page on that node with no test to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The new `getForLogin` caching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` includes a recovery branch where a cached internalId resolves to `null` via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, triggering `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` and a delegate reload. The added test `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin` verifies cache population and invalidation for create/remove/update scenarios, but it never creates the specific condition of a stale cached internalId that no longer resolves (i.e., a "poisoned" cached ID set). So the fallback/self-healing path is not exercised or verified by any test in this diff. The cluster-wide propagation concern is speculative, but the missing coverage for this new non-trivial recovery branch is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The newly added `idp.isEnabled()` re-filter in both branches of searchForIdentityProviders — added because a wrapped/cached IDP can appear in getForLogin results while disabled — has no test in the diff verifying that a disabled-then-cached IDP no longer renders on the organization login page. Other callers of getForLogin that don't re-check isEnabled (any broker-selection path outside this bean) still receive the disabled IDP from the cached stream; nothing in this diff pins the contract of which layer is responsible for the enablement check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `idp.isEnabled()` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)` in both branches (the `ORG_ONLY` and `ALL` `getForLogin(...)` calls) with an explicit comment that the returned IDP "might have been wrapped." However, the only new/expanded test in the diff (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercises `getForLogin` caching/invalidation and counts of returned IDs; it does not cover the Freemarker bean path nor assert that a disabled IDP that could be present in `getForLogin` results is filtered out from the organization login page rendering. So the advisory about missing test coverage for this newly added filtering logic is grounded in the diff. The broader concern about other `getForLogin` callers receiving disabled IDPs is plausible but not directly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The getLoginPredicate change (requiring orgId==null or BROKER_PUBLIC config) silently alters the semantics of getForLogin for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation and every caller of the predicate, not just the caching layer this PR claims to add. Storage providers with no cache (e.g. map/JPA in non-cached setups) and any other consumer of getLoginPredicate (admin/console listing, other SPI callers) now exclude organization-linked non-public IDPs that were previously returned; this is a cross-cutting behavior change not traceable to the 'add caching support' requirement, and it is hidden inside what looks like a cache-only diff — additionally, idp.getConfig() returning null for a model with an organizationId throws NPE inside the predicate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` globally by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This is a cross-cutting behavioral change affecting any caller/implementation using this shared predicate (not just the new Infinispan caching logic), which is a legitimate scope/architecture concern grounded in the diff. However, the finding’s claim that this is definitively a BUG (i.e., incorrect behavior) isn’t provable from the diff alone, and the asserted NPE on `idp.getConfig()` can’t be verified here because the contract of `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` (nullability) isn’t shown in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) while the cache-miss path maps results through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the returned stream has different semantics depending on cache state. The first uncached call after invalidation returns organization-wrapped IDP models (which can override enabled/visibility per organization context), while all subsequent cached calls return unwrapped raw models — callers like OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean get different data for the identical request depending on whether the cache was warm; the method does not enforce the invariant that its result shape is independent of cache state.

adjudication.rationale: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them directly without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (see the final `return identityProviders.stream();`). From the diff alone, this means the same getForLogin request can yield wrapped (organization-aware) models when uncached, but unwrapped models when cached, violating consistent semantics across cache state as described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual generated alias "idp-alias-" + i, and duplicates it for every loop iteration. getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) either throws EntityNotFoundException during cleanup or is a silent no-op for all 21 created IDPs, leaving test data in the shared test realm and polluting subsequent tests that read realm IDPs via the new login caches.

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the loop creates IDPs with aliases `"idp-alias-" + i`, but registers cleanup with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal "alias"). This is duplicated each iteration and does not correspond to the created resources, so the created IDPs will not be removed by this cleanup (and may even fail during cleanup if no IDP named "alias" exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update-path invalidation optimization (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) relies on the assumption that the organizationId field and BROKER_PUBLIC config on the passed models capture every way an IDP's login eligibility can change, which the diff does not establish. Any write path that mutates login-relevant state without passing through this provider's update() (e.g. organization link changes driven through OrganizationProvider's own broker update, or direct config changes by other SPIs) leaves the .idp.login caches serving stale IDP lists until an unrelated invalidation; the skip-fast branch converts a previously-always-fresh lookup into a staleness window that the new test only exercises through the admin API.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the update-path optimization compares `getLoginPredicate()` on original vs updated models and also checks `Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())` before skipping invalidation. `getLoginPredicate()` itself (modified in this diff) incorporates `organizationId`/`BROKER_PUBLIC` plus all other `LoginFilter` conditions, so within this provider’s `update()` path the optimization is tied to the same predicate used to determine login eligibility. The finding’s main concern (login-relevant mutations happening via other write paths that bypass this provider’s `update()`/`create()`/`remove()`, e.g., organization link changes through other SPIs) is not demonstrated or verifiable from the diff alone; those external mutation paths are asserted but not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw (unwrapped) IdentityProviderModel objects while the delegate path wraps each result with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so the same call returns differently-behaving models depending on whether the entry was already cached. The login page's IDP list changes behavior between the first (uncached) request and every subsequent (cached) request after the cache warms: organization-aware wrapping (which the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean diff explicitly acknowledges alters visibility/enabled semantics — 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped') is missing on the cached path, producing different IDP lists and enabled flags for the same realm/org depending on cache state.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, explicitly wrapping each `IdentityProviderModel`. However, the cache-hit path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, this makes the method’s return type/behavior inconsistent depending on cache state (wrapped vs potentially unwrapped models), matching the finding’s core claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate arm `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, and getConfig() can be null for programmatically created IdentityProviderModel instances. Any IDP with an organizationId set but a null config map makes getLoginPredicate().test(idp) throw NullPointerException, breaking every caller of getForLogin/getLoginSearchOptions for that realm, including non-cached storage providers that now inherit the new predicate arm.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new arm to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that unconditionally calls `idp.getConfig().get(...)` when `idp.getOrganizationId() != null`. If `getConfig()` can ever be null, this would introduce an NPE in `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` and thus impact callers of `getForLogin(...)` that rely on this predicate. The diff itself shows the dereference without any null-guard; however, whether `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The change to getLoginPredicate silently alters the results of getForLogin for ALL IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations (including JPA/Map with no cache), not just the new caching path — org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC=true are now excluded by a shared SPI predicate where the filtering was previously the caller's concern. Existing deployments and any in-tree or out-of-tree caller that relied on getForLogin returning org-linked non-public brokers (e.g. custom login UIs, OIDC well-known endpoints) see their IDP lists shrink with no version bump or migration note; behavior is baked into the SPI rather than the FetchMode/caller layer where ORG_ONLY vs ALL semantics live.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the shared SPI-level predicate: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` now adds `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. Any code path (in-tree or custom) that relies on this predicate to define “login-eligible” IDPs will now exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, regardless of whether the caller intended that to be enforced at the FetchMode/caller layer. While the diff doesn’t show every `getForLogin` implementation, the finding’s core concern (semantics shifted into a shared SPI utility) is directly supported by the change in `server-spi` and is a nontrivial scope/compatibility issue rather than a purely internal cache change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove(alias) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a delegate/DB query) before the cache-validity check, even in the branch where the cached entry was previously sufficient for the internalId invalidation. Every alias removal pays an uncached delegate lookup it did not pay before, solely to feed registerIDPLoginInvalidation; in a single-node Map storage setup this converts a cache-served admin operation into a hot DB hit, and when the IDP is not found the storedIdp passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidation is null (handled, but the wasted query remains).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)` (and before reading `CachedIdentityProvider` from the cache). Previously, the delegate lookup happened only in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch; the cache-valid branch could invalidate using cached data without a delegate/DB hit. The new unconditional delegate call is only used to feed `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, and `storedIdp` may be null (handled because `getLoginPredicate()` starts with `Objects::nonNull`), but the extra lookup is still paid. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A single cache entry keyed by (realm, FetchMode) accumulates a searchKey->IDP-set map for every organizationId ever queried, with whole-entry rebuild (invalidateObject + full delegate reload + addRevisioned) on each first query for a new org and whole-entry invalidation on any IDP change, so entry size and rebuild cost grow linearly with the number of organizations. A realm with many organizations (Keycloak targets org-heavy tenants) gets one ever-growing cache object that is fully reloaded from the delegate each time a new org's login page is first hit, and fully invalidated (cold reload for all orgs) on any single IDP create/update/remove of a login IDP — a thundering-herd style scalability cliff on the login path the cache was meant to accelerate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new cache for `getForLogin` keyed only by `(realmId, FetchMode)` via `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`, and stores per-organization results inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry using `searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` and `query.getIDPs(searchKey)`. When a new `organizationId` is first queried and `cached == null`, the code invalidates the whole cache key (`cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`), reloads from the delegate, and writes a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` that appears to carry forward the prior query while adding the new org’s result. This implies one cache entry can accumulate many org-specific ID sets over time, and each new org causes whole-entry invalidation + reload for that org. Separately, create/update/remove of a login-qualifying IDP invalidates the entire login cache for all modes (`for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values()) realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(...))`), wiping all accumulated org mappings. This is a scalability/architecture concern (cache growth and churn on login path), not a correctness defect visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two cache-population branches are asymmetric: the first uses addRevisioned(query, startupRevision) while the second (searchKey miss on an existing entry) uses cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) after having captured loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey) in between an invalidateObject and the re-add, so the revision embedded in the query and the version used for the re-add can disagree. If the counter raced with a concurrent cluster invalidation between getCurrentRevision and getCurrentCounter, the entry is installed with a version that makes subsequent invalidation checks (isInvalid comparisons against the embedded revision) pass for stale data, leaving a login page serving pre-invalidations IDP lists; the inconsistency between the two branches also invites drift on the next copy of this pattern.

adjudication.rationale: The asymmetry described is real in the diff: in `getForLogin`, the initial population path builds `IdentityProviderListQuery` with `loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)` but stores it via `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “searchKey miss” path does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`, then captures `loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)`, embeds that in the new `IdentityProviderListQuery`, and stores it via `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This means the revision embedded in `IdentityProviderListQuery` can differ from the revision used to version the cache entry, and the two branches use different versioning strategies. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify the claimed stale-data bug because the semantics of `addRevisioned`, `getCurrentRevision/getCurrentCounter`, and `isInvalid()` are not shown; the finding is a credible, diff-grounded correctness concern but not provably a defect based only on this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" (get("alias")::remove) instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so it targets a nonexistent identity provider. The 20 created IDPs (and later idp-alias-20) are never removed by cleanup, polluting the test realm for subsequent tests and, depending on the admin client, causing the cleanup itself to throw a 404/NullPointerException during test teardown.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (and again after creating `idp-alias-20`). The literal `"alias"` does not match any of the created IDPs, so the intended IDPs are not removed during teardown, potentially leaving test data behind and/or causing teardown failures when attempting to remove a non-existent IDP.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The shared SPI's getLoginPredicate() was silently redefined to exclude organization-linked identity providers lacking BROKER_PUBLIC, changing the semantics of getForLogin for every storage provider and caller, not just the caching layer. This PR's stated intent is adding caching; instead it alters core login-visibility semantics for all implementations (JPA/map/legacy) and any other caller of getLoginPredicate() — org-linked private IDPs that previously appeared in getForLogin results for their own organization members disappear, with no human sign-off that the objective expanded from caching to a behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the shared SPI predicate `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This is a global semantic change (affects all `getLoginPredicate()` callers/implementations, not just the Infinispan caching provider) that will exclude any organization-linked IDP whose config lacks/has false `BROKER_PUBLIC`. Whether that behavior change is desired can’t be proven from the diff alone, but the finding is correct that the SPI behavior is broadened beyond “just caching” and can impact non-cache storage providers and callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The login page bean now filters out IDPs whose wrapped model reports isEnabled()==false, changing which identity providers render on the organization login page. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel instances that are disabled (e.g. private org brokers) were previously passed to createIdentityProvider and now vanish from the login page for all users; this is a user-visible login-page behavior change bundled into a caching PR without explicit acceptance of the changed objective.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders` adds an extra filter `idp -> idp.isEnabled()` in both code paths, whereas previously it only filtered out `existingIDP` by alias. This is a concrete, user-visible behavior change in which any `IdentityProviderModel` whose `isEnabled()` returns false will no longer be passed to `createIdentityProvider(...)` and thus won’t render. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that such disabled/wrapped IDPs were intended to be shown (the added comment suggests this is a deliberate correctness guard: "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped"), so calling it a definite bug is not supported solely by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cached-hit path of getForLogin returns IDPs fetched via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the cache-miss and invalidation fallback paths do wrap, so the same request returns differently-shaped (non-organization-aware) models depending on cache state. The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean already had to re-check isEnabled() 'as idp might have been wrapped' (companion hunk in this diff); on cache hits the login page instead receives unwrapped models whose organization-linked behavior (e.g. redirect/alias handling for org members vs. the public broker config gated by BROKER_PUBLIC) is lost, so an end user hitting the login page after a cache populate gets different/broken broker options than a user on the cold path.

adjudication.rationale: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin, the cache-miss path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, and the invalidation fallback path does the same. However, on a cache hit it iterates cached IDs and returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` directly (`identityProviders.add(idp); return identityProviders.stream();`) without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes returned model types/behavior depend on cache state, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate arm 'idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))' dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check and without consulting the organization provider's isBrokerPublic() logic, hard-coding the visibility rule into the storage SPI. Any IdentityProviderModel implementation (custom storage/legacy import) whose getConfig() returns null throws NullPointerException from getLoginPredicate, breaking every getForLogin call including the login page; and future changes to org-broker visibility semantics must now be replicated in two places (OrganizationProvider and this SPI predicate), risking a normalization-mismatch where the org provider treats an IDP as public while the login predicate does not, silently hiding it from the login page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` the arm `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, which dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check and inlines the broker-public rule directly into the SPI predicate. From the diff alone, it’s verifiable that a null `getConfig()` would NPE and that the visibility semantics are duplicated here rather than delegated to an organization/provider API. However, the diff does not establish whether `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is contractually non-null or whether `OrganizationProvider.isBrokerPublic()` exists/should be used, so the “will break every getForLogin call” claim can’t be confirmed as a definite defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When an existing IdentityProviderListQuery lacks the requested organizationId searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then re-adds a merged query using cache.getCurrentCounter() as the revision rather than the startupRevision used on first population, so concurrent readers on other cluster nodes can observe a revision/counter pairing the invalidation protocol does not expect. Under concurrent logins against different organizations in a clustered deployment, a stale query object resurrected from the local Infinispan cache can be re-added with a revision that is not the session's startup revision, allowing the merge path to re-insert entries containing IDP ids invalidated earlier in the same transaction; users then see removed or disabled identity providers on the login page until the next full invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the initial population stores `IdentityProviderListQuery` with `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but the merge path (when `query != null` and `query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null`) does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then re-adds the merged query with `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That inconsistency in the revision source (startupRevision vs currentCounter) is directly shown in the diff and could affect the cache invalidation/revision protocol in clustered/concurrent scenarios, but the diff alone doesn’t prove the concrete stale-resurrection behavior described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test registers cleanup against the wrong alias literal "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) dereferences a non-existent IdentityProviderResource. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns a resource for a nonexistent IDP; the cleanup remove() throws a 404 (or the resource is null causing an NPE), failing the test during cleanup and leaving the 20 created IDPs behind to pollute subsequent tests in the realm.
matched_golden_ids: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue points out that cleanup uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the dynamically created alias "idp-alias-" + i, which is exactly the golden issue about incorrect alias usage in cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new test never exercises the 'query exists but searchKey not cached' branch of getForLogin (the cached == null path that calls cache.invalidateObject, getCurrentRevision, and addRevisioned with cache.getCurrentCounter()). Every getForLogin call in the test uses the same organizationId per FetchMode, so the multi-organization sub-map merge path — which also uses getCurrentCounter instead of the startupRevision used by the first branch — is completely unverified; a regression there (stale or dropped IDP lists for a second organization hitting a warm cache) would ship unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the `cached == null` branch is only reached when a cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists for a given `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` but the specific `searchKey` (derived from `organizationId` or "") has not yet been stored in that query, triggering `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and re-adding via `cache.addRevisioned(..., cache.getCurrentCounter())`. In the added `testCacheIDPForLogin`, every `getForLogin` invocation uses the same `organizationId` (`orgaId`) for `FetchMode.ORG_ONLY` and `FetchMode.ALL`, and `null` ("" searchKey) for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY`, so it never calls `getForLogin` for a *second* organization under the same `FetchMode` after the query is cached. Therefore the multi-searchKey merge/revision path is indeed untested, which is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for newly added caching logic rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test discards the return value of every session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) call and only asserts internal cache-query sizes, never the stream contents or their organization-aware wrapping. The caching layer could return wrong IdentityProviderModel instances (wrong models resolved by internal ID, missing createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping) or take the cache-miss fallback path (idp == null) and the test would still pass, since only the cache object's set sizes are checked — the actual user-visible behavior is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, the calls to `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` are not consumed/collected; the test then only asserts `IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(...).size()` from the cache (`realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKeyForLogin(...))`). This verifies cache population/invalidation and ID set sizes, but it does not verify the returned `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` contents (e.g., correct IDs resolved back to models) nor the organization-aware wrapping applied on the cache-miss path (`idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`). So it is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The isEnabled() re-check added to both filter chains in searchForIdentityProviders has no test in this diff that asserts a disabled-but-wrapped IDP is excluded from the login page. The stated reason for the change ('idp might have been wrapped' by the caching layer returning a model that bypasses the delegate's enabled filtering) is exactly the scenario the new test should cover but doesn't — OrganizationCacheTest never renders the login page nor asserts enabled/disabled filtering through the bean, so a regression reintroducing disabled IDPs on the org login page would pass the suite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavioral guard in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders()` by filtering with `idp.isEnabled()` (twice) with the explicit rationale that an IDP “might have been wrapped” by caching. The only added test (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercises `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` caching/invalidation and asserts cache contents, but it never calls `searchForIdentityProviders()`, never renders/validates the login-page IDP list, and does not assert that a disabled-but-wrapped IDP is excluded. So the finding that this new enabled-filtering logic is not directly covered by tests in this diff is accurate and specific to the changed lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The change to getLoginPredicate silently reclassifies every existing org-linked identity provider without a BROKER_PUBLIC config entry as unavailable for login, with no backfill or migration step for stored IDP configs. Deploying this against existing realms drops all org-linked brokers that never had BROKER_PUBLIC explicitly set from every login page and every consumer of getLoginPredicate at once; operators see brokers disappear from the login screen with no data change, no migration, and no way to tell from the diff which existing rows are affected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `BROKER_PUBLIC` to be `true` for any org-linked IDP: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. Since `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` is `false`, any existing org-linked IDP whose config lacks the `BROKER_PUBLIC` key will no longer match the login predicate, affecting all consumers of `getLoginPredicate()` and the new caching around `getForLogin()`. The diff shows no migration/backfill logic for existing stored IDP configs, so the finding about a silent behavior change on upgrade is grounded. Whether this is a "bug" depends on intended semantics, which the diff alone can’t prove; it is at least a concrete upgrade/compatibility concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration in testCacheIDPForLogin fetches the nonexistent alias "alias" (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so get("alias") returns null and the cleanup method reference throws NullPointerException during teardown. Both IDP-creation loops (lines ~390 and ~432) register a cleanup against a provider that does not exist, so test teardown throws an NPE and the 20+ created identity providers are never removed, leaking state into subsequent tests in the same realm.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, both places where new IDPs are created register cleanup with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (inside the `for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++)` loop and again after creating `idp-alias-20`). The created IDPs have aliases like `idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19` and `idp-alias-20`, so the cleanup targets the wrong alias and will not remove the created providers, leaking state into later tests. Whether this also throws an NPE depends on the admin client behavior, which is not shown in the diff, but the incorrect alias and cleanup leak are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In getForLogin's not-yet-cached-searchKey branch, the new IdentityProviderListQuery is added with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the initial-population branch uses the session's startupRevision, so the incrementally-added search entries are revisioned differently from the initial entry for the same cache key. A reader that populated a different searchKey for the same realm+fetchMode key gets a differently-revisioned query entry; if the revisioned-add semantics of getCurrentCounter do not match startupRevision-guarded invalidation, subsequent invalidations from registerIDPLoginInvalidation can leave a stale searchKey's IDP set live after an IDP is removed, serving a removed broker on the organization login page until the whole entry is evicted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an inconsistency in how the same cache key is revisioned in `getForLogin`: the initial population branch does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the "searchKey not yet cached" branch creates a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(...)` and then does `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This difference is real and diff-grounded. However, the claimed stale-data behavior depends on the (not-shown) semantics of `addRevisioned`, `startupRevision`, `getCurrentCounter()`, and `registerInvalidation`, so the concrete defect scenario cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidation dereferences the passed IdentityProviderModel through getLoginPredicate (idp.getOrganizationId(), idp.getConfig()) without a null check, and in update() the idpById lookup result can be null when the internalId does not resolve. An update() call whose getById(internalId) returns null (e.g. alias was already removed, or an ID with no backing row) throws NullPointerException from the added predicate chain instead of the no-op that the pre-existing registerIDPInvalidation(null) path tolerated, turning a previously-benign update into a 500 for admins.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` is explicitly null-safe: it begins with `((Predicate<IdentityProviderModel>) Objects::nonNull).and(...)`, and `Predicate.and(...)` short-circuits, so `idp.getOrganizationId()` / `idp.getConfig()` are not evaluated when `idp` is null. In `update()`, even if `idpById` is null, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)` calls `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` (returns false) and all subsequent dereferences of `original` are guarded by short-circuit (`pred(original) && ...`), so no NPE is introduced by this change. The finding’s claimed NPE path is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate stage `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` throws NullPointerException whenever an IDP has a non-null organizationId and a null config map (IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns null when no config was ever set). Any call path that evaluates getLoginPredicate() — including the cache provider's create()/update()/remove() invalidation logic — crashes with NPE instead of completing; an admin creating/updating or a login flow listing IDPs for a realm where an org-linked IDP was imported without a config map gets a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(...))` to `getLoginPredicate()`, which would NPE if `idp.getConfig()` were null. However, the PR diff does not show the contract/implementation of `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` or any evidence that it can return null, and the finding asserts this as a definite crash scenario based on behavior not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cached hit path resolves IDs via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while the two delegate paths in the same method do apply it, so the returned model shape depends on whether the list query was already cached. Users hitting the warm cache get plain IdentityProviderModel instances while cold-cache users get organization-aware wrapped instances; any consumer relying on the wrapper's overridden behavior (e.g. the enabled flag re-check added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) sees different results for the same request depending on cache state.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(...) the cold/invalid-cache paths return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel), but the warm-cache hit path iterates cached internal IDs and returns session.identityProviders().getById(id) directly, without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (see the final return identityProviders.stream()). This makes the returned IdentityProviderModel differ depending on cache state, so consumers can observe inconsistent behavior for the same request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares the updated model against `original` obtained from getById() which is served from the IDP-level Infinispan cache, so the skip decision is made on a possibly stale snapshot of the stored IDP. If the cached original is stale (e.g. a recent change from another node has not yet been reflected), the predicate comparison can wrongly conclude login-availability is unchanged and skip invalidating the login caches, leaving the login IDP list stale across cluster nodes until an unrelated invalidation fires.

adjudication.rationale: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, the new logic calls `IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId());` and then uses that `idpById` as the `original` input to `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model)`. Given this class is the Infinispan caching storage provider, `getById()` is very likely to be served from cache (not shown in the diff), so the skip/return decisions inside `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` can be made based on a potentially non-authoritative snapshot. The diff does not prove this can occur (cluster invalidation semantics and `getById()` implementation aren’t included), so it’s not verifiable as a definite bug from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/architecture concern about correctness of invalidation decisions in a clustered environment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Each distinct organizationId encountered for a given FetchMode causes the entire cached IdentityProviderListQuery to be invalidated (cache.invalidateObject) and rebuilt with the previous entries merged, so the single cache entry accumulates an unbounded per-org map and every new org's first login request evicts-and-rebuilds the entry for all orgs. In realms with many organizations, the first login per org pays a full delegate query plus a cluster-wide invalidation of the shared key, and the query object's internal map grows linearly with org count — cache churn and memory growth that degrade exactly the hot login path this diff intends to speed up.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s new caching in `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)` uses a single cache key per realm+mode (`cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)`). When a cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but lacks the current `searchKey` (derived from `organizationId`), the code explicitly does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then rebuilds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` (note the last `query` parameter), which implies carrying/merging prior entries while adding a new per-searchKey entry. This matches the finding: per new orgId (searchKey) the first request triggers invalidation/rebuild of the shared entry, and the query object can accumulate entries per org, implying linear growth and cache churn on the login path. This is a performance/scalability concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The defensive re-check added to both branches only re-checks idp.isEnabled(), not the other criteria of the login predicate (hideOnLogin, org BROKER_PUBLIC), so a wrapped model that was made login-ineligible by any non-enabled criterion still passes the filter. A login page served from the cached getForLogin path can render an IDP that hideOnLogin or org-visibility rules exclude, and clicking it proceeds into a broker flow the admin explicitly hid — inconsistent with the predicate the cache is supposed to honor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new defensive filter in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `idp.isEnabled()` (explicitly noted in the comment), but there is no diff-grounded evidence that the cached `getForLogin` path can return IDPs that violate the login predicate (e.g., `hideOnLogin` or org `BROKER_PUBLIC`). In fact, `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)` populates the cache from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, which is the API expected to already apply the full login predicate, and update/remove/create paths add targeted invalidation (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`) based on `getLoginPredicate()` changes (including the newly added `BROKER_PUBLIC` condition). The finding assumes the bean’s extra filter is meant to enforce the full predicate and that caching can bypass it, but that behavior is not shown in the diff.
